title: Profitable hotel chain Bloom raises Rs 700 crore from Kedaara, eyes Southeast Asia next
summary: Hotel chain Bloom raised 700 crore rupees from Kedaara to expand regionally
detailed: Delhi-based hospitality brand Bloom has raised $75 million or nearly Rs 700 crore in a primary funding round led by private equity firm Kedaara Capital, as it plans to grow its hotel portfolio to 12,000 rooms over the next few years, from more than 4,700 expected by March 2027.
In FY25, Bloom's revenue from operations rose about 36% to Rs 357.50 crore, from Rs 262.60 crore a year earlier.

According to media reports, Samena Capital, founded by Shirish Saraf, was the hotel chain's largest investor before the Kedaara deal, having invested around Rs 362 crore and held a majority stake in the company.

In June 2025, Bloom's board approved the issue of 7.77 crore compulsory convertible preference shares to raise Rs 77.7 crore from Samena Capital and Ikonika Holdings, according to a RoC filing reported at the time.
sentences: Delhi-based hospitality brand Bloom has raised $75 million or nearly Rs 700 crore in a primary funding round led by private equity firm Kedaara Capital, as it plans to grow its hotel portfolio to 12,000 rooms over the next few years, from more than 4,700 expected by March 2027.
The startup runs hotels under brands including Bloom Hotel, Bloom Hub, BloomSuites and Bloomrooms.
Bloom describes itself as a tech-driven travel and hospitality brand.

It said it built its own cloud-based technology platform before it took on its first hotel, and that the platform has allowed it to expand while keeping service standards consistent across properties.
Part of the new funding will go into that platform, particularly into AI and dynamic pricing, which the startup said will improve the customer experience and operational efficiency.

“ We look forward to working with the outstanding Kedaara team, ” said Sanjeev Sethi, President of Bloom, adding that the aim was “ to build Bloom into one of Asia's iconic brands. ”
“ The tech build-out will remain our primary focus in delivering consistent value across the Bloom platform every single time, ” Sethi said.

Anant Gupta, Partner at Kedaara Capital, said, “ We see an exciting opportunity for Bloom to emerge as one of India's most differentiated and loved consumer brands. ”
Bloom expects to operate more than 4,700 rooms by the end of the current financial year in March 2027.
It aims to reach 12,000 rooms across its key markets over the next few years before it enters new geographies, with a focus on domestic and outbound travel.
The target is roughly 2.5 times its expected size at the end of this financial year.
Bloom said it has grown at a compound annual rate of about 30% over the past five years while staying profitable.
The startup's last reported annual numbers show that pattern.
In FY25, Bloom's revenue from operations rose about 36% to Rs 357.50 crore, from Rs 262.60 crore a year earlier.
EBITDA stood at Rs 75.01 crore and profit after tax at Rs 15.20 crore.
That works out to an EBITDA margin of roughly 21% and a net margin of about 4%.
Revenue has grown about six times in three years, from Rs 58 crore in FY22.
Room revenue made up 85% of total income in FY25, food and beverages 13.1% and other income 1.9%.

At the time of those results in October 2025, Sethi, then the company's COO, said Bloom aimed to keep revenue and profit growth in the 30-35% range in the coming years without compromising capital efficiency.
The startup said then that it onboards only about one in 20 hotels that apply to join it, and that more than 75% of its hotels were in Tier 1 cities.
Bloom was co-founded by Gobind Singh Akoi.

According to media reports, Samena Capital, founded by Shirish Saraf, was the hotel chain's largest investor before the Kedaara deal, having invested around Rs 362 crore and held a majority stake in the company.

In June 2025, Bloom's board approved the issue of 7.77 crore compulsory convertible preference shares to raise Rs 77.7 crore from Samena Capital and Ikonika Holdings, according to a RoC filing reported at the time.
The startup was also reported to be looking to raise Rs 400 crore from private equity investors.
At the time, Bloom had more than 50 hotels across cities including Mumbai, Pune, Udaipur, Jaipur and the NCR.
It competes with Treebo Hotels, FabHotels, newer players such as Salt Stayz, and Oyo through its Sunday Hotels brand.
Bloom is raising funding as hotel development in India picks up outside the big metros.
According to the HVS Anarock India Hospitality Industry Overview 2025, nationwide hotel occupancy was 63-65% in 2025, with average daily rates of about Rs 8,500-8,700.
Hotel brands signed about 64,118 rooms across 586 properties during the year, while around 14,199 rooms across 176 properties opened.
The report said Tier 2, Tier 3 and increasingly Tier 4 markets are becoming central to the next phase of growth.
